messages:
eva: New hires hitting failures running unit tests. Vitest -> 'Unexpected token export' from node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js. Jest in CI shows ERR_REQUIRE_ESM.

noah: Classic ESM/CJS friction. Are they deep-importing or using named imports?

eva: Tests import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'. We tried Vitest deps.inline and an alias to a local shim, which fixed Vitest locally. CI Jest still fails.

rachel: Short checklist that helped other teams: (1) Jest: add transformIgnorePatterns to include the SDK package so babel/ts-jest can compile it, e.g. "/node_modules/(?!@redwood-inference/sdk)"; (2) If using ts-jest, enable useESM and extensionsToTreatAsEsm; (3) For Vitest, deps.inline + resolve.alias to a CJS shim works; (4) As SDK team we should publish a CJS build or test-utils mock entrypoint.

eva: We used jest.mock('@redwood-inference/sdk', () => ({ createClient: jest.fn(), __esModule: true })) which helped in some tests but not when module evaluated before mock. jest.isolateModules helped.

sdk-bot: Created issue #421: "SDK: test-runner compatibility (Jest/Vitest)" assigned @noah  https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/421

noah: Will add a small example in SDK repo: sample Jest & Vitest configs, note on Node options (--experimental-vm-modules), and recommend a test-utils factory for mocking. That should smooth onboarding.

eva: Thanks. I'll add the shim to the onboarding repo for now and link the issue.
